messages:
katie (prod): Heads-up — product wants the ability for a tenant to pin a model via an HTTP header (tenant controls model alias/version for a route). Use case: enterprise customers that validated a quantized variant and require it for compliance. Thoughts? :thinking:

saul (eng-platform): Important Qs: precedence vs existing routing rules, and should pinning be allowed only on dedicated/private customers? Also how do we prevent arbitrary header spoofing?

alex (eng-runtime): We can support an opt-in header like `X-Redwood-Model-Alias`. Behavior proposal: if header present and tenant allowed, try to resolve alias -> model_version. If incompatible with route constraints (max_seq, tokenizer mismatch), reject with 422 + structured error. Fallback policy: `header -> route-config pin -> global alias` then normal routing.

tanya (devex): UX: need console toggle per-tenant and clear audit trail for who pinned what and when. Also suggest showing warnings in the console if the pinned model increases latency/cost.

yusuf (sre): We'll need telemetry tags for pinned=true/alias=... for SLO slicing. Also quota enforcement — pinned variants still count against same quota buckets? If dedicated pools, maybe separate metering.

saul (eng-platform): On spoofing: require the header only on authenticated requests where the token belongs to tenant X and tenant X has policy `allow_header_pin: true`. Block for public API keys.

alex (eng-runtime): Implementation sketch (route matcher snippet):
```yaml
route_match:
  api_prefix: /v1/generate
  tenant_allow_header_pin: true
  model_compat_constraints:
    - tokenizer: gpt2
    - max_seq: 8192
fallback_policy:
  - header_alias
  - route_pin
  - model_catalog_default
error_responses:
  incompatible: {code: 422, message: "Pinned model incompatible with route constraints"}
```

saul (eng-platform): Nice. Need to define precedence precisely and how this surfaces in the routing decision graph. Also what about function-calling/streaming compatibility with quantized variants?

alex (eng-runtime): Precedence proposal (definitive):
1) Tenant-enforced pin via route config (highest)
2) Authenticated header alias (if enabled for tenant)
3) Per-route alias mapping (classic)
4) Global default model for route
If header resolves to model with missing capability (e.g., no streaming), runtime returns `capability_mismatch` with suggestions (e.g., use non-quantized alias).

tanya (devex): For console: add a small banner when users toggle header-pinning: "Header pinning bypasses automatic rollouts; pinned tenants won't receive canary updates unless you update the pin." Also give a one-click revoke.

yusuf (sre): Telemetry plan: add fields `routing.pinned=true/false`, `routing.pinned_alias`, `routing.resolution_source` (header|route|default). Add metric `pinned_request_count` and split latency histos by pinned vs not.

ops-bot: feature-flag created: `routing.header_model_pinning` set to `off` in staging. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/512 :eyes:

katie (prod): OK action items: (1) eng-runtime to draft RFC for compatibility checks + error codes; (2) eng-platform to add tenant policy + precedence docs; (3) devex to mock console flows and audit UI; (4) sre to propose telemetry metrics. Catch-up sync tomorrow 10:30. :+1:

saul (eng-platform): I'll add precedence table to the routing docs and a note about ACLs. Will also add tests to ensure header can't be used with public API keys.

alex (eng-runtime): I'll start an RFC and include the YAML examples + unit tests for capability mismatches.

tanya (devex): I'll mock the UI and the warning text, share Figma link in this thread when ready.

yusuf (sre): I'll stub dashboards for pinned vs unpinned slices so we can validate after feature flag flip.

katie (prod): Great, thx everyone.
